---
title: "Week 2 application: interactions are not automatically simplices"
subtitle: "A small complex-systems example"
toc: true
---

## Scientific question

Suppose six oscillators are represented by a network whose edges record
sufficiently strong pairwise coupling. Does a triangular group of pairwise
couplings represent a genuine three-way interaction, or only three separate
pairwise relationships?

This matters because the two interpretations produce different simplicial
complexes and may produce different homology.

## Observed and constructed objects

The observed data might be simultaneous time series together with estimated
pairwise coupling strengths. Those estimates produce a weighted graph. The
graph is already a constructed representation: its edges depend on the
coupling estimator and threshold.

There are then at least two possible topological objects:

1. the graph treated as a one-dimensional complex, containing vertices and
   edges only; or
2. its clique complex, which fills every mutually connected triple with a
   2-simplex and continues similarly in higher dimensions.

The clique complex makes the additional assertion that pairwise coherence is
enough to infer a coherent multiway unit. That may be appropriate for a
pairwise-generated interaction mechanism, but not for every complex system.

## Small inspectable example

Let oscillators $a,b,c$ have all three pairwise edges. As a graph, the chain
$ab+bc+ca$ is a non-boundary cycle and contributes one $H_1$ class. In the
clique complex, the 2-simplex $abc$ is added and

$$
\partial_2(abc)=ab+bc+ca
$$

over $\mathbb F_2$. The same edge cycle is now a boundary, so its homology
class vanishes. Nothing about the observed edge set changed. The representation
choice changed.

## Baseline and sensitivity

Before interpreting homology, report graph quantities such as connected
components, degree distribution, clustering and graph cycle rank. Then vary
the coupling threshold and the rule for filling cliques. The main comparison
is not “topology versus no topology”; it is graph-only structure versus an
explicit higher-order representation.

## Interpretation boundary

A filled triangle means that the construction treats the three oscillators as
one coherent multiway relation. It does not prove that the physical system has
an irreducible three-body interaction. That claim requires a mechanistic or
statistical argument beyond the simplicial calculation.

::: {.callout-note title="Planned data extension"}
This page deliberately uses six labelled oscillators so every simplex and
boundary can be checked by hand. A later real-data extension should use a
public coupled-oscillator or functional-connectivity dataset, state how edges
are estimated, and compare graph and clique-complex conclusions under the same
thresholds.
:::
